 Judgment
In this appeal, the insurance company challenged the judgment and award dated 01.03.2012 passed in MVC No.520/2007 by the Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Ranebennur (for short

,
'Tribunal').
2. The appellant was the second respondent, respondent Nos.1 to 4 were the petitioners and respondent No.5 was the first respondent before the Tribunal.

Hence, for the sake of convenience,
rankings of NC: 2024:KHC-D:7725 the parties shall be referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are Holiyamma (the deceased) is the mother-in-law of first petitioner and grandmother of petitioner Nos.2 to 4, on 25.01.2007 at 10.15 a.m. she met with an accident on Medleri Ranebennur road while crossing the road hit by a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-27/J-1718 causing her injuries.
She was admitted to the Government Hospital, Ranebennur.
In spite of treatment, she succumbed to death on 26.01.2007.
The petitioners claiming that they are the dependents approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-.
That the deceased was aged 60 years, doing agriculture and earning Rs.6,000/- p.m.
Claim was opposed by the respondents.

The Tribunal after holding enquiry and hearing on both the sides, by the impugned The Divisional Manager vs Hanumavva W/O Lakshmappa Kadimani on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92679998/
2 judgment, awarded the compensation of Rs.2,80,000/- with 6% NC: 2024:KHC-D:7725 interest.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Challenging the same, the insurance company has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel Sri G.N. Raichur appearing for appellant and learned counsel Sri G.N. Narasammanavar appearing for petitioners.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for insurance company that the deceased was aged 97 years, she was blind and totally depended on the petitioners.
In spite of the same, the Tribunal considered the petitioners as dependants and assessed the compensation which is contrary to the evidence on record.
Utmost, the petitioners may be entitled for loss of estate and accordingly he sought for modification of the impugned judgment and award.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the age of the deceased was 60 years, she was doing agriculture and earning more than Rs.6,000/- p.m.
In spite of that, the Tribunal has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.4,000/- p.m. NC: 2024:KHC-D:7725 only and assessed the lesser compensation.
The deceased was not blind and not aged 97 years.
The Tribunal is right in assessing the dependency and in awarding compensation.
He sought for enhancement of compensation and dismissal of the appeal.
7. I gave anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both the sides and perused the records.
8. There is no dispute with regard to the accident, cause of accident, death of the deceased on account of accidental injuries.
It is pertinent to note that the deceased was aged and the petitioners are the daughter- in-law and grandchildren.
Before the Tribunal, third petitioner has stepped into the witness box and during the course of cross-examination, he has admitted that the deceased was aged 97 years and she was blind.
This shows that a lady aged 97 years cannot work and do not get any income.

Even assuming for the purpose of assessing compensation she was earning some money, having regard to her age, the petitioners being majors, the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7725 deceased must have been the dependent on the petitioners and not the petitioners were the dependents on the deceased.
Hence, utmost the petitioners being the daughter-in-law and grandchildren are entitled to claim incidental expenses and also loss of estate.
9. On perusal of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal without giving any reasons, directly come to the conclusion that the deceased was earning and petitioners were her dependants.
As the material on record clearly point out that the age of the deceased was 97 years and it is hard to accept that she was an earning member.

The accident is of the year 2007 and the notional income of the deceased can be taken at Rs.4,000/- p.m., if 50% of the said income is deducted towards personal expenses then it comes to Rs.2,000/- and if multiplier of 5 based on the age of the deceased is applied, the probable dependency comes to Rs.1,20,000/-.
Out of this, if 25% is considered as loss of estate, the petitioners are only entitled for Rs.30,000/-.

The total compensation comes to Rs.80,000/-.
Compared to the Tribunal, award of Rs.2,80,000/- is on the higher side.
Hence, the appeal deserves to be allowed.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The judgment and award dated 01.03.2012 passed in MVC No.520/2007 by the Addl.
